tsx transpiles each file on the fly with esbuild, so it's fast and handles ESM/CJS interop for you, but it does no type checking at all. ts-node uses the real TypeScript compiler, so it type-checks by default (slower, unless you switch to transpile-only or swc), and its ESM support has historically been the fiddly part. In practice that means tsx for running scripts, with `tsc --noEmit` still needed as a separate check.
Action: nothing to change; I'll keep typecheck as its own step and can add a script for it in packages/cli if you want.

A 403 CSRF failure on hx-post after moving the form into a partial usually means the request isn't carrying the token anymore. Common causes are that the partial's form lacks `{% csrf_token %}` (having it in the base template doesn't cover a form that is swapped in), or that the partial is rendered without the request so the tag outputs nothing. A global fix is `hx-headers` on the body sending `X-CSRFToken`.
Action: I'd look at the partial and the view that renders it, check the rendered HTML for the csrfmiddlewaretoken field, and then add the tag or the body-level hx-headers; can you paste the partial?
